title: Canonical monoidal derived pullback of pro-etale internal modules
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, $X,Y$ schemes, and $f:X\to Y$. Put $\mathcal C_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\operatorname{Ab}))$, where $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $F=f^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\operatorname{Ab}}):\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and $LF:D(\mathcal C_Y)\to D(\mathcal C_X)$ its total unbounded left derived functor [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Give these derived categories the relative derived tensor products [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules]. Then $LF$ is strong monoidal [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Its comonoidal tensor comparison
$$\delta_{M,N}:LF(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_Y}N)\longrightarrow LFM\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}LFN$$
is the universal left-derived tensor comparison of the ordinary monoidal pullback. Explicitly, writing $Q_T:K(\mathcal C_T)\to D(\mathcal C_T)$ for localization, $F_h$ for termwise pullback, $\gamma:LFQ_Y\Rightarrow Q_XF_h$ for its derived counit, $\mu_T:Q_TA\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_TB\to Q_T(A\otimes B)$ for the localization tensorator, and $m_{A,B}:F_hA\otimes F_hB\xrightarrow{\sim}F_h(A\otimes B)$ for the ordinary tensorator on homotopy complexes, define
$$r_{A,B}=Q_X(m_{A,B})\circ\mu_X\circ(\gamma_A\otimes\gamma_B),\qquad l_{A,B}=\gamma_{A\otimes B}\circ LF(\mu_Y).$$
Both are natural transformations to $(A,B)\mapsto Q_XF_h(A\otimes B)$ and exhibit their respective source bifunctors as total left derived bifunctors. The universal comparison $\delta$, characterized by $r_{A,B}\circ\delta_{Q_YA,Q_YB}=l_{A,B}$, is invertible. Its comonoidal unit map $LF(\mathbf1)\to\mathbf1$ is $\gamma_{\Lambda_Y[0]}$ followed by $Q_X$ of the ordinary unit comparison $F(\Lambda_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X$ in degree zero. All assertions hold for arbitrary $\Lambda,f$ and unbounded complexes.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(3), Proposition 6.8.11(3); canonical derived tensor construction as formalized by new-integral-residue-derived-monoidal

proof.text: For $T=X,Y$, use the essentially small pro-etale site in the coefficient universe, as specified in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed], $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\operatorname{Ab})$ is Grothendieck abelian, with additive closed symmetric sheafified tensor. The category of abelian groups has the functorial flat epimorphism $\mathbf Z[|A|]\to A$, $[a]\mapsto a$: tensoring a free group is a direct sum of copies of the identity and preserves exact sequences. Thus [lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution] applies to $\mathcal A_T$. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] and [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions] with the commutative ring object $\Lambda_T$. The relative tensors and their symmetry are [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor], and [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] makes them closed. They are additive: their defining coequalizers [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] are cokernels of differences of the two action maps, and tensor and cokernel maps are additive. Hence $\mathcal C_T$ is a monoidal Grothendieck abelian category with functorial flat resolutions, with exactly the relative tensor required in the statement.

source.place: Opening sentence: the closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck module category with functorial flat resolutions

proof.text: The functor $F$ is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], is a left adjoint by the adjunction clause of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and is strong monoidal by [new-integral-residue-ordinary-monoidal], whose first assertion is for arbitrary condensed $\Lambda$, not only integral coefficients. The map $\alpha_f:f^*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$ is an isomorphism by [def-sfb-alpha]. Set $R=\Lambda_Y$, $S=\Lambda_X$, and $\rho=\alpha_f^{-1}:S\to f^*R$. Clause 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] gives $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\rho}$, hence $F\cong\operatorname{mapModComap}(\rho)$. Apply [new-proetale-inverse-image-module-flat] with these $R,S,\rho$. This is exactly preservation of flat internal modules for the relative tensors, and it transfers through the natural isomorphism because exactness is invariant under conjugation by isomorphisms. All the hypotheses of the generic derived monoidal construction are now verified.

source.place: Tag 05VD, lemma-pullback-flat, applied through the internal-module flatness statement; coefficient identification is blueprint def-sfb-alpha and change-of-scalars clause 5

proof.text: We also need actual K-flat images for the two-variable universal-property test. The transport part sends K-flat complexes to K-flat complexes by [lem-sfb-module-mapmod-pullback-kflat]. Extension along the isomorphism $\alpha_f$ is a strong monoidal equivalence, with inverse restriction along $\alpha_f$, by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] and the balanced-tensor formula in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]: relabelling scalars identifies both coequalizer action arrows. For any acyclic complex $N$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules and K-flat complex $P$ over $f^*\Lambda_Y$, the complex $\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f}N$ is acyclic since restriction along an isomorphism leaves the underlying abelian sheaves and differentials unchanged. The tensor $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}P\otimes_{\Lambda_X}N$ identifies with $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}(P\otimes_{f^*\Lambda_Y}\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f}N)$, which is acyclic; the same holds with the factors reversed. This is K-flatness by [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Thus $F_h$ sends K-flat complexes to K-flat complexes.

source.place: K-flat construction of the full composite module pullback; scalar change is along the coefficient isomorphism

proof.text: Since $F$ is a left adjoint, [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] applies to each countable direct sum defining total tensor. On its $(p,q)$ summand define $m_{A,B}$ by the ordinary tensorator $FA^p\otimes FB^q\to F(A^p\otimes B^q)$ followed by $F$ of the summand inclusion. Naturality of the ordinary tensorator [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] with $d_A^p$ and $d_B^q$ identifies the two differential contributions with $F(d_A^p\otimes1)$ and $(-1)^pF(1\otimes d_B^q)$. Additivity of $F$ preserves the sign and their sum. This proves the chain-map equation for the differential of [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy]. Applying the inverse ordinary tensorator and the inverse direct-sum comparison gives the inverse chain map. The same naturality formula with arbitrary cochain maps proves naturality in both variables; with a degree-minus-one homotopy it identifies the boundary $dh+hd$, so the maps pass to homotopy classes. Thus $m$ is the indicated natural isomorphism on $K(\mathcal C_Y)$. This also identifies it with the degreewise concrete comparison, without assuming an unproved chain-map claim from the upstream file.

source.place: Total tensor of complexes and its passage to homotopy classes; tensorator construction expanded on each bidegree

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] and [lem-sfb-derived-tensor-modules-derived], $Q_T$ is lax monoidal and $\mu_T$ is the two-variable derived tensor counit. By [def-sfb-left-derived-functor], $LF$ has a natural counit $\gamma_A:LF(Q_YA)\to Q_XF_hA$; [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], exact-functor clause, identifies $LF$ with termwise $F$, the termwise functor already inverts quasi-isomorphisms, so its counit is an isomorphism by the derived universal property. Hence $\gamma_A$ is invertible for every $A$. Define $h_{A,B}=\mu_{X;F_hA,F_hB}$ followed by $Q_X(m_{A,B})$. Define $r$ by tensoring $\gamma_A,\gamma_B$ and then applying $h$, and define $l=LF(\mu_Y)$ followed by $\gamma_{A\otimes B}$, as in the statement. These are natural in each variable: for $a:A\to A'$, the equations $Q_X(F_ha)\gamma_A=\gamma_{A'}LF(Q_Ya)$ and naturality of $\mu_X,m$ move $a$ through each factor of $r$; naturality of $\mu_Y,\gamma$ does the same for $l$. Replacing $a$ by $b:B\to B'$ gives the other two laws. Their compositions therefore define genuine natural transformations of bifunctors.

source.place: Localization tensor counit and its naturality; unary derived counit of the full composite in the parent unit

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-kflat-derivability] to $\mathcal C_Y$. The required colimits are present by its Grothendieck property, and closedness makes tensor preserve them by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Use its K-flat inclusion in both variables of [lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus]. The target $T(A,B)=Q_XF_h(A\otimes B)$ inverts coordinate quasi-isomorphisms on K-flat pairs: tensoring has that property by the definition [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], and exact $F$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms by the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. On K-flat $P,Q$, step 3 makes $F_hP,F_hQ$ K-flat; therefore $\mu_X$ is invertible by [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal], as is $r_{P,Q}$. Also $\mu_Y(P,Q)$ and $\gamma_{P\otimes Q}$ are invertible, so $l_{P,Q}$ is invertible. The candidate criterion in [lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus] now proves that both source bifunctors, with their specified counits $r,l$, are total left derived bifunctors of $T$. In particular there is a unique comparison $c$ from the source of $l$ to the source of $r$ with $r\circ c=l$. The reverse universal comparison is its inverse: both composites have the identity's composite with the respective counit, so uniqueness makes them identities.

source.place: Two-variable derived universal property tested on K-flat pairs; the comparison isomorphism and uniqueness

proof.text:
Apply [new-integral-residue-derived-monoidal] to the categories and functor checked in steps 1 and 2; this is its general $F$ assertion, before its integral specialization. Let $\delta$ be the comonoidal tensorator of its strong monoidal structure on $LF$. The precise counit equation is [new-integral-residue-derived-monoidal-counit]:
$$\mu_X\circ(\gamma_A\otimes\gamma_B)\circ\delta_{Q_YA,Q_YB}=Q_X(m_{A,B}^{-1})\circ\gamma_{A\otimes B}\circ LF(\mu_Y).$$
Postcompose with $Q_X(m_{A,B})$. Functoriality cancels $Q_X(m)Q_X(m^{-1})$, giving exactly $r\circ\delta=l$. By the uniqueness from [lem-sfb-multivariable-derived-calculus], $\delta=c$, so the universal comparison is the comonoidal tensor map, with its actual specified counits. Step 4 gives equality with the concrete summand-defined $m$; hence it also identifies $h,r,l$ componentwise with the concrete upstream homotopy and two derived counits. No replacement of a counit by an arbitrary isomorphic one is involved.

source.place: Descending the ordinary tensorator and identifying its counit normalization by the two-variable universal property

proof.text:
Write $I_T=\Lambda_T[0]$ and $e_F:F_hI_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}I_X$ for the ordinary unit comparison in degree zero. Set $e=Q_X(e_F)\circ\gamma_{I_Y}:LF(\mathbf1)\to\mathbf1$. It is invertible: $\gamma$ is invertible by exactness [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and $e_F$ is an isomorphism [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. The unit of $Q_T$ is the identity on $Q_TI_T$, and its unit coherence follows from [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal], whose unit constraints are induced from complexes. Evaluate the counit equation of step 7 at $(I_Y,B)$; use the left-unit equation for the ordinary $m,e_F$ and the left-unit equation for $\mu_X,\mu_Y$. Naturality of $\gamma$ with the left unitor then gives, after cancellation of the isomorphism $\gamma_B$,
$$\lambda_{LF(Q_YB)}\circ(e\otimes1)\circ\delta_{\mathbf1,Q_YB}=LF(\lambda_{Q_YB}).$$
At $(B,I_Y)$ the right-unit equations give $\rho_{LF(Q_YB)}\circ(1\otimes e)\circ\delta_{Q_YB,\mathbf1}=LF(\rho_{Q_YB})$. Every derived object is represented by a homotopy complex, so these identities hold for all objects. Keep the associative tensorator $\delta$ of step 7 and use these unit identities: $\delta^{-1},e^{-1}$ meet precisely [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. This constructs the required strong monoidal structure with the explicit unit map in the statement.

source.place: Unit constraints induced from complexes, applied to the exact module pullback; explicit derived-counit normalization
